thread:
olivia_support: Heads-up: ACME reported a bunch of traces where the frontend `request_id` doesn't link to any spans in Trace Explorer. They see an HTTP 502 returned to clients but our trace shows only the root span, no downstream spans.
ryan_eng: Can you paste the request_id and approximate time?
olivia_support: request_id=acme-req-20260314-7b2f, occurred ~2026-03-14T15:12Z. Customer attached a screenshot of the trace panel with just a single node.
miguel_sre: Quick check — are these coming from the lightweight proxy path that strips headers? We've seen `x-request-id` rewritten before.
olivia_support: Customer says their `x-request-id` is preserved in the frontend logs. They also sent nginx access log snippet: 
```
2026-03-14T15:12:03Z frontend-1 GET /api/pay 502 "x-request-id: acme-req-20260314-7b2f"
```
ryan_eng: Can you also share the SDK call payload that forwards downstream spans? Wondering if the client is using the async flush path.
olivia_support: They pasted the fragment: `client.send({trace: true, request_id: 'acme-req-20260314-7b2f'})` and said they upgraded SDK last week.
hao_product: Does the customer mention any recent rollout or changed config? Might be related to new continuous-batching defaults.
miguel_sre: If the process crashed before KV cache commit or before spans were flushed, you'd see root recorded but not children. Any crash logs?
ryan_eng: I repro'd locally with a forced SIGTERM during a bursty workload and see the same pattern. The child spans are buffered in the worker and flushed on a final ack. If the worker dies we only get the initial span.
olivia_support: Customer says they also saw a `503` from our internal model backend around the same time. Logs: `modelpool-2 2026-03-14T15:12:02 ERROR backend timeout`
ryan_eng: Ok, hypothesis: backend timeout causing the forwarding agent to abort the flush. Steps to repro: 1) run a burst of requests, 2) inject latency or timeout at model backend, 3) kill worker before flush. I'll create a small repro harness.
miguel_sre: In the meantime, add a defensive flush on error path to reduce orphaned child spans. Also add a metric for "span-flush-failures" so we can alert.
hao_product: Agree — we should surface this in Console observability: a chart that shows % of traces with missing child spans by model/service.
olivia_support: Customer is asking for ETA on root cause and mitigation. Can we give a short workaround?
ryan_eng: Workaround: enable immediate-span-flush feature flag on their private deployment (config `trace.flush_on_error=true`). That will increase token overhead but should recover links.
miguel_sre: I'll file an internal JIRA: RINF-8342 for durable flush on error + metric + alert.
hao_product: Also flag for docs update and note in changelog.
olivia_support: I'll relay workaround + timeline to ACME and keep thread updated. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Ticket created RINF-8342 (P2) — assigned to ryang.
ryan_eng: Starting on repro now, will paste steps + minimal harness here when ready.
olivia_support: Marking customer escalated; will keep monitored until mitigation deployed.
